texts: Write a verse about the man who scrubs the stone floor of his house every morning until it shines, yet never sweeps out the spite and greed that clutter the corners of his mind.
You scrub the stone of your house till it gleams, yet leave the dust of envy lying in your mind.
My aunt cleans her house three times a day, stone floors and all, but still carries a grudge in her mind she has not aired in years.
stone house, clean mind
doha on scrubbing the stone house clean but not the mind
You wash the skin a hundred times, yet the mind that moves within stays stained; cleanse that instead.
clean mind, not clean skin
Compose a doha about the person who bathes carefully every day and dresses in spotless clothes, but whose mind is full of envy, anger, and deceit, and who has never thought to clean it.
A man in our town is always spotless and perfumed, and also the cruelest talker in the whole neighbourhood.
doha about washing yourself every day but keeping a dirty mind
Write a doha about the man who wears the whitest cotton and is proud of its cleanliness, though his thoughts are stained by greed and jealousy that no washing can remove.
cotton, clean inside
My uncle wears crisp white cotton every day and still cheats his own brother over the family land.
doha on white cotton clothes but dirty thoughts
The cotton is washed white, but the thought is dyed dark; whiten the thought and the cloth may stay as it is.
Make the heart clear, O seeker, and no ritual will be needed; the clear heart shows its own God.
Give me a verse about the quiet beauty of a mind that is free from malice, envy, and deception, and about how this inner cleanliness matters more than any outer rite of washing.
doha on keeping my mind clean not just my body
purity of heart
I realised last week that I scrub my hands compulsively but let angry thoughts run through my head all day without a thought.
Not the washed face but the faithful heart, not the shining skin but the stainless thought, is clean.
clean heart, clean mind
My grandmother says she has never taken a ritual dip in a holy place but her thoughts have always been clear, and I believe her.
Compose a doha that says true cleanliness is not in how often you wash the outer body, but in whether your mind and heart are free of dirt like anger, lust, greed, and pride.
what makes a person truly clean? doha
doha on arrow and jaggery, words from a clean mind
Write a doha about words that leave the mouth like arrows, wounding when they come from a dirty mind but sweet as jaggery when they come from a heart that has been cleaned of envy and anger.
arrow, jaggery, clean mind
The arrow of speech flies from a clean bow or a crooked one; sweet as jaggery are the words of a clear heart.
My father never says a harsh word, and his sentences melt like jaggery, and I think it is because there is no malice in him at all.
A bee keeps landing on my clean-hearted friend's hand while he works in the garden, and it seems as if even creatures sense a stainless nature.
The bee seeks only the clear nectar; to the clean heart come the sweetest flowers.
Write a verse about the bee, which settles only on clean blossoms, and the person with a heart cleansed of malice, who attracts sweetness and good company wherever he goes.
bee doha on a clean mind
bee, clean mind
On the bier the body is washed; what you take with you is the cleanliness of the mind.
At my grandfather's bier, relatives washed his body with such care, and I wondered whether anyone had cared as much for the cleanliness of his thoughts.
doha on the bier: what matters is a clean mind not a clean body
Compose a verse about how the body is washed and perfumed for the bier but only the cleanliness of the mind we cultivated in life accompanies us when we depart.
bier, clean mind
moneylender, clean intentions
The moneylender counts every coin but never counts the dirt of greed in his own mind.
moneylender doha on clean intentions
Our local moneylender bathes twice a day and wears spotless clothes while cheating poor farmers on every loan.
Write a doha about the moneylender who dresses in white and washes his hands before every meal, yet whose mind is stained by greed and whose dealings are never honest, and who has never cleaned that.
tongue, traveler, clean heart
doha on a sweet tongue and dirty heart: the traveler is lost
A guest with a charming tongue stayed with us last month, so neatly groomed, but his heart had room for nothing but scheming.
Compose a doha about the traveler who comes with a smooth tongue and fair words, but whose heart is full of deceit, and who is therefore never really at rest, however clean his appearance.
The tongue that speaks sweetly while the heart is dirty is a traveler lost in a perfumed fog.
oil press mosque doha clean mind

Write a verse about the believer who washes his hands and feet before entering the mosque, yet does not wash the oil press of his thoughts that grinds out resentment, and who prays with a stained heart.
He washes before the mosque and leaves the oil press of resentment running in his mind.
oil press, mosque, clean heart
Every Friday my neighbour washes carefully before the mosque, and every Saturday he is back to grinding the same bitter grudges.
The lion is brave, the lamp is bright, but only a spotless mind gives the true flame.
My uncle was strong as a lion and burned like a lamp for the whole family, and he had a heart with no malice in it at all.
Write a doha about the lion that rules by fear and the lamp that gives clear light, and how the person with a purified mind has both strength and brightness without any stain of cruelty.
doha on a lion and a lamp, clean mind
lion, lamp, pure mind
cremation ground doha about being clean inside
At the cremation ground all bathing ends; only the cleanness of the heart accompanies the soul.
After the cremation ground, everyone washed in the nearby tank, and I wondered who among them had cleaned their mind of its grudges.
cremation ground, clean heart
Compose a verse about the cremation ground where all outer washing is useless, and how a person's real purity is judged only by the freedom of his heart from envy and deceit.
Musk deer, the cloth sheet is stained, but your scent is pure; so let my mind carry no dirt, though the cloth is plain.
musk deer, cloth sheet, pure
Write a doha about the musk deer that carries its scent without ever washing and the poor man in a plain cloth sheet whose heart is clean, who are both pure in ways no bathing can match.
A poor man in a worn cloth sheet at our gate had a heart as clean as a musk deer's scent, and his kindness filled the room.
doha on a cloth sheet and a musk deer: purity is inside
doha on a philosopher's stone and a thorn: purify the mind
Write a verse about the philosopher's stone that transforms base metal and the thorn that stays in the heart, and how the true alchemy is to remove spite and cleanse the mind until it is clear.
The philosopher's stone turns iron to treasure, but only a cleansed mind pulls out the thorn of envy.
I would give a philosopher's stone to be rid of this thorn of jealousy lodged in my mind, which no washing could ever remove.
philosopher's stone, thorn, clear heart
The palace is marble-clean while the mind of the king is a muddy lane; sweep the inner hall first.
palace doha about a clean mind
Our local rich man's palace is the cleanest in the district, but he is the most anxious and suspicious man I know.
palace, clean mind
Compose a verse about the king in the spotless palace whose servants scrub every floor but whose own mind is cluttered with suspicion, greed, and pride, which no one can sweep for him.
Wiping the mirror and washing the milk jug every morning, I thought how little I clean the thing that really needs it, my own mind.
Write a doha about the mirror that must be wiped clean to show a true face and the milk that sours in a dirty cup, and how the mind must be purified to hold anything good.
Look in the mirror of the mind; if it shows a clear face, drink the milk; if not, wash the mirror first.
mirror, milk, clean heart
doha on mirror and milk: a clean mind
After the monsoon the leaves in my yard looked brand new, and I wished my mind could be rinsed so easily of its old resentments.
A leaf washed by the rain is green and clear; so is the heart rinsed of all spite.
leaf doha on a clean heart
leaf, clean heart
Write a verse about the leaf which is cleaned by the rain without any effort of its own, and about the mind that becomes clean when it lets go of anger and envy and stands quietly under grace.
The moth worships the glow with clean wings, and dies singing; a stainless heart makes a pure end.
Compose a doha about the moth which flies to the glow with nothing in its heart but longing, and the person whose mind is as clean of malice, giving himself entirely to what he loves.
I watched a moth circle a glow with a single purpose, and wished my own mind were as free of petty thoughts as that little creature.
moth, pure heart
doha on the moth: pure of heart
Cleanse the thoughts, O friend, for the body forgets its washing by evening, but the mind remembers its stains.
Write a verse about the old question of whether one should work harder to keep the body clean or the mind clean, answering that thoughts are the deeper dirt which no soap in the world can reach.
clean the mind
clean mind or clean body, which matters? doha
I spend an hour grooming each morning, but not one minute checking whether my thoughts are kind.
doha on the washerman who cleans clothes but not himself
washerman, clean inside
Compose a doha about the washerman who leaves everyone else's clothes spotless but whose own mind is full of petty envies and little deceits, which no ghat can wash away.
The washerman in our colony is proud of his work, but I see him whispering spite about the very families whose clothes he cleans.
The washerman beats the dirt from every cloth; who will beat the dirt from his own mind?
ritual dip, unclean thoughts
i washed in the holy dip but still feel dirty inside, doha
What use is the ritual dip, if the thought remains unclean? Cleanse the thought and the dip is done.
Give me a verse about the person who takes the holy dip at every festival and returns with the same angry, envious mind, learning at last that purity comes not from ritual but from a change of heart.
My cousin visited the holiest pilgrim places this year, and came back exactly as petty as he was before.
The priest recites the cleanest verses with the dirtiest thoughts; the Lord hears only the mind.
priest, clean mind
Our priest keeps his dhoti spotless and his chants flawless, but I have seen him counting the offering plate with a very greedy look.
priest doha on clean mind
Write a doha about the priest who keeps himself spotlessly clean and chants perfectly, but whose mind is full of greed for offerings, which the Lord notices more than any amount of ritual.
Compose a verse about the gentle shine of a mind that has let go of envy, malice, and deceit, whose very presence makes others feel at ease, and who needs no outer ritual to prove his purity.
There is a woman at my workplace who has never gossiped about anyone, and just being around her makes my mood lighter.
doha on keeping the mind clean
A clean mind needs no scrubbing; it shines of its own accord, and everything it touches grows clearer.
clear mind, clear speech
Write a verse about the one-string lute which sounds sweet only in a clean hand and the leaf that drops without a stain, and how the stainless mind alone makes true music of a simple life.
leaf, one-string lute, stainless
leaf and one-string lute doha: clean heart
The leaf falls clean upon the strings; only the pure heart plays the one-string lute without discord.
An old man with a one-string lute sat in the courtyard as a leaf drifted down onto it, and his music was so clean that no one spoke.
doha on a palace and a fly: unclean inside
The palace is scrubbed from roof to floor, but the fly settles where the heart is stained.
The palace-like mansion of my boss never has a speck of dust, and yet the fly of his bitterness hovers around every conversation.
palace, fly, clean heart
Compose a doha about the king whose palace is so clean that not a fly can settle on its walls, yet whose heart is so dirty with envy that it attracts every kind of trouble.
milk, palanquin, pure heart
milk and palanquin doha: pure mind
Pure as milk the heart must be, though it ride in a palanquin or walk in the dust.
Write a verse about the bride in the palanquin dressed in white, and the milk poured out as an offering, and how the heart must be as clean as both for the offering to be accepted.
The bride in the palanquin looked like she was made of milk, and I overheard her whisper to her sister that she had forgiven everyone that morning.
net and touchstone doha: purity of mind
The net of the mind catches many kinds of thought; only the touchstone of truth shows which are clean.
Write a doha about the net of thoughts that gathers clean and dirty alike and the touchstone that tests which is stainless, and how the wise man keeps only the pure and throws back the rest.
Each night I cast a net over my day's thoughts and test them against what I truly believe, and I always find a few that need to be thrown away.
net, touchstone, clean mind
mosque, bier, clean heart
Compose a verse about the man who washes at the mosque and is washed again for the bier, and who must in the interval wash his heart of the only stain that matters, the grudge against his neighbour.
My father washed at the mosque five times a day and was washed again for his bier, and I hope he cleaned his heart in between.
Washed before the mosque prayer, washed again for the bier; only the heart's own cleaning carries across.
doha on mosque and bier: cleanness of heart
what does pure of heart even mean? doha
Give me a verse about the meaning of a pure heart, one that has no spite, no hidden plan, no secret envy, and no bitterness, and about how such a person feels light and at ease in the world.
A teacher of mine had no malice in him whatsoever, and being around him felt like stepping into relief after a long day.
Pure are those whose hearts hold no knot; they walk lightly through life.
a clean heart
sandalwood, pure mind
A friend of mine, with a mind free from all malice, makes everyone in the room feel calm, like a whiff of sandalwood in a hot afternoon.
Compose a doha about sandalwood, which perfumes whatever touches it, and the mind that is free from malice and so soothes all who come near, without the need of any outer show.
doha on sandalwood and a pure mind
Sandalwood cools with its own scent; the pure mind cools whoever comes near, without a word.
The hands are clean, the mind is stained; wash the thoughts, O friend, for there lies the dirt.
washing my hands again and again but my mind feels unclean
I washed my hands twenty times a day last winter and I still felt unclean until I forgave my brother.
wash the mind
Write a doha for the person who washes and scrubs and still feels unclean, telling him that the stain is in thought and resentment, and that only forgiveness and honesty can wash it away.
doha on a fly and a clean mind
A fly kept landing on my sticky desk, and I thought of how petty thoughts also gather around a mind I haven't cleaned in a long time.
The fly seeks out the sore, the pure heart has none; be a clean wound-free mind, and no fly will come.
Write a verse about how a fly settles only where there is something unclean, and how the person with a clear and clean mind attracts no flattery, no envy, and no scheming.
fly, clean mind
short doha on being honest and clean inside
No fold in the heart where a falsehood might hide; this is the clean life.
honest, clean within
Give me a verse about a heart so open and honest that there is nothing hidden and nothing to be ashamed of, and about the peace of living with a mind that has nothing to conceal.
I told my wife the whole truth about the mistake I made, and I felt a long stain leave my mind.
Write a doha about the heart full of old grudges and the moment when forgiveness cleans it out, leaving a freshness and ease that no outer washing could ever give.
rinse the heart
doha about letting go of grudges to feel clean
After I forgave my sister last month, I felt as if a window had been opened in my chest and a breeze had come in.
Rinse the heart of its old grievances, and make it ready to be filled again with something sweet.
Write a verse about the shroud that wraps every body in the same white and the stars that watch, with only one thing shining beyond the body, the purity of the heart that was kept clean in life.
doha on stars and a shroud: the clean heart matters
Under the stars at a village funeral, I watched them wrap the shroud around a man whom everyone called clean-hearted, and no one cried louder than his enemies.
stars, shroud, clean heart
Under the stars, in the shroud, all are equal; only the clean heart shines when the body is wrapped.
Our neighbour wipes his front gate twice a day but fights with everyone in the lane, and I wonder where he should really be cleaning.
inner cleanness
Without a clean mind, all other cleaning is a show; with a clean mind, no other cleaning is needed.
Compose a verse about how all outer cleaning without inner purity is only a show, while the person who has cleaned his mind has no need to prove his cleanliness to anyone.
doha: there's no point in outer cleanness without inner
The pearl is born clean in its shell, the salt cleanses all it touches; the pure heart is the pearl of the self.
doha on pearl and salt: pure mind
My mother-in-law keeps a pearl necklace in a drawer and a pinch of salt in every prayer, and says the cleanest thing is the mind.
pearl, salt, stainless
Write a doha about the pearl that grows clean in the shell and the salt that cleanses, and how the heart too must be rid of its impurities to become a gem shining without stain.
how do i get a pure mind?
I started noting each unkind thought at night, and after a few months my mind felt so much lighter and clearer.
Give me a verse about the long, gentle practice of cleansing the mind of envy, anger, and craving, until it becomes as clear and still as a calm morning, in which everything is seen truly.
Let the heart be clear and still, with no mud stirred up, so that all truth is reflected in it.
purify the mind
dirty mind, cleanse it
Compose a doha for the person who feels stained inside by envy, spite, and old deceptions, telling him that this dirt cannot be scrubbed off but only released through honesty and a change of heart.
What washing can cleanse the envy in the mind? Only the simple washing of truth and forgiveness.
doha: i feel dirty inside, how to clean the mind
I keep thinking mean thoughts about people I actually love, and I feel dirty in a way no shower can fix.
My best friend has never said anything behind my back that he wouldn't say to my face, and that makes him the cleanest person I know.
Clear are the thoughts that harm no one; clear the speech that hides nothing; clear the one who is both.
Write a doha about the unity of clean thought and clean speech, where a person's mind and mouth are one, with nothing hidden and nothing twisted, and whose presence brings ease.
doha on clear thoughts and honest speech
clear thoughts, clear speech
clean clothes, dirty thoughts
Write a doha about a person who spends his money on spotless clothes and flawless grooming, yet carries a mind soiled by jealousy and contempt, which no tailor or barber can set right.
My cousin gets compliments for his crisp, immaculate clothes while thinking mean things about everyone in the room.
doha: dirty thoughts, clean clothes
The outside is spotless, the thought is soiled; who will launder the mind?
how do you bathe the mind?
Compose a verse about the daily bath of the mind, where one washes away anger with patience, envy with gratitude, and pride with silence, until the mind is clean and light by evening.
The bathing of the mind is done in silence, with forgiveness and honesty.
bathe the mind
Each night I sit quietly and let go of the day's grudges one by one, and by the end I feel washed all over.
The elephant is tied with a rope of its own habit; cut the rope, clean the mind, and walk free.
rope, elephant, pure mind
doha on a rope and elephant: clean the mind
Like an elephant tied to a thin rope, I stayed bound by an old resentment I could have dropped the moment I cleansed my mind.
Write a verse about the elephant tied by a thin rope of its own old habits and the seeker whose mind is bound by old dirt, who must cut the rope and cleanse himself to walk free.
I donated generously last year, but looking back, I did it for the applause, and I could not feel clean about it afterwards.
clean motives
doha on clean motives
Give me a verse about how the cleanliness of our motives matters more than the outward form of our deeds, and how a kind act done with a hidden selfish aim is stained from the start.
Not the deed but the reason behind it, the hidden motive, must be clean for the result to be good.
doha on smearing ash but unclean heart
ash, clean heart
Compose a doha about the sadhu who smears himself with ash and looks holy while his heart is stained by anger and desire, and how true holiness requires cleansing the inner life.
Ash on the brow is nothing if the heart under it is unclean; wash the heart first.
A man in my town smeared with ash looks very holy, but he screams at his wife at night over trifles.
Write a doha about the grindstone that wears away the coarse and the heron that stands white and still, and how the mind must be ground clean of roughness and kept as white and quiet.
grindstone and heron doha: pure mind
The grindstone grinds off the coarse husk of the heart, and the heron stands white and still in the clear shallows.
grindstone, heron, pure heart
The old grindstone in our courtyard wore the husk off grain, and a heron outside was so white and still that I felt my own mind needed grinding clean.
My neighbour's house is spotless with a heavy lock on every entrance, and yet his mind seems to be full of dirt and worry.
doha on a clean house, but a messy mind

Write a doha about the man who keeps his house meticulously swept and puts a strong lock on every entrance, but whose mind is full of dust and cobwebs of envy, which he has never even thought to clean.
A house swept clean, a strong lock on the gate, and the mind unlocked and dusty within; sweep the mind first.
house, lock, clean heart
house, milk, pure heart
In a clean house the milk stays sweet; in a clean mind, every thought stays sweet.
Compose a verse about the clean house where milk stays fresh and sweet and the clean heart where thoughts stay fresh and sweet, and how both need daily care for the home within to remain pure.
doha: clean house and pure milk, but what about the mind
In my grandmother's house the milk never spoilt, and neither did her mind, which she cleaned every night by forgiving everyone.
A friend once said that a pure mind is more valuable than any philosopher's stone, and her own gentle presence proved it.
Write a doha about the legendary philosopher's stone and the purified mind, and how the true transformation happens in a heart cleansed of envy and greed, whose touch brings sweetness.
The philosopher's stone changes iron to treasure, but a pure mind changes every touch to blessing.
philosopher's stone doha on a pure mind
philosopher's stone, pure mind
